Build a music streaming platform for iOS, Android and Web that meets these business objectives:
BO-1: Users play music on iOS, Android and Web, with at least 9,000 concurrent users at launch and a UAT score of at least 4.2/5.
BO-2: Users find and organize music through search, recommendations, playlists and a personal library.
BO-3: Users interact with music and other listeners through Live Premiere, live chat, favorites, ratings, comments and notifications.
BO-4: Administrators manage songs, albums, artists and user accounts from the Flutter Web admin dashboard.
BO-5: User accounts and personal data are protected and recoverable, with daily backups meeting RPO 24 h and RTO 4 h.
BO-6: The platform can scale and be maintained after handover: up to 50,000 concurrent users in future phases and a 1-year warranty.

Develop a music streaming platform delivered as mobile apps (iOS and Android) and a Flutter Web client for end-users, all built on a single Flutter codebase, with Vietnamese and English GUI. The system uses a client-server architecture with a Node.js (Express.js) backend API and a PostgreSQL database, supporting registration/login and profile management, online and offline music playback, live premiering music, rating, comments and favorites, playlist and library management, search and song recommendations, and a Flutter Web-based admin dashboard with CRUD operations for songs, albums, artists and user accounts.

In scope: iOS and Android mobile apps and a Flutter Web client for end-users, built on a single Flutter codebase, with Vietnamese and English GUI options. Backend: a Node.js (Express.js) API, PostgreSQL database, and WebSocket-based real-time messaging for Live Premiere, covering authentication, data management, and CDN-based content delivery. Core user functions: registration/login and profile management; music playback and live premiering music; rating, comments and favorites; playlist management, library management, offline download; search and recommendations; in-app purchases via App Store / Google Play billing. Also includes a Flutter Web-based admin dashboard with CRUD operations for songs, albums, artists and user accounts, a 1-year post-launch warranty covering technical support and system maintenance, and the lifecycle from requirement gathering and system analysis through UI/UX design, frontend/backend development, QA testing and final deployment.
Out of scope: separate native codebases for iOS and Android; processing payments directly (own gateway, card details or e-wallets); native desktop apps; designing subscription plans; multi-language GUI options beyond Vietnamese and English; product marketing; music content licensing; User Acceptance Testing (performed by the Customer on staging); customer support and maintenance beyond the 1-year post-launch warranty period.

- System design (architecture, detailed design, ER diagram, general API specification in OpenAPI 3.0) and UI/UX mockups

- Test reports (integration, security, device and load testing at 9,000–15,000 concurrent users) and test summary report

- The server supports at least 9,000 concurrent users at launch and up to 15,000 with an error rate < 1%.
- Backend API response latency < 200ms for 90% of queries. App launch speed: cold start < 2s, warm start < 1s.
- App battery consumption < 6% per hour, tested with audio streaming over Wi-Fi, screen turned off, volume at 50% on a device with ~4,000 mAh battery capacity.
- Secure user accounts: passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor >= 10); authentication via JWT access/refresh tokens (access token expiry <= 1 hour); all client-server traffic over TLS 1.2 or higher; refresh tokens stored via platform secure storage (Keychain / Keystore / httpOnly cookie on Web).
- UI/UX follows Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Google Material Design 3, with a UAT satisfaction score >= 4.2/5.
- The system architecture must be containerized and designed to horizontally scale to support up to 50,000 concurrent users for future phases.
- Backend REST API documented with the OpenAPI 3.0 specification; all endpoints versioned under /api/v1.
- Automated backend test coverage of at least 70%; PostgreSQL backed up daily with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 24 hours and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 4 hours.
- Centralized logging and uptime monitoring for all backend services, with alerting on error-rate and latency threshold breaches.

Risk level: Medium. Key risks:

Project Title: Development and Deployment of a Music Streaming Platform

Build and deploy a music streaming application for iOS, Android and Web that lets users discover, listen to, rate and comment on music and manage their favorite music on their devices. The system uses a client-server architecture with a Node.js (Express.js) backend API and a PostgreSQL database. A team of 5 members delivers it in 5 months (August 17, 2026 - January 15, 2027) with a budget of 757,000,000 VND.
Product scope:
- Clients: iOS and Android apps and a Flutter Web client for end-users, built on a single Flutter codebase to reduce development cost and time and keep one UI; GUI in Vietnamese and English.
- Backend: Node.js (Express.js) REST API and PostgreSQL for API management, user authentication and data queries; WebSocket real-time messaging for Live Premiere; audio and music-video files kept in object storage and served through a Content Delivery Network (CDN); PostgreSQL stores only application data and media metadata.
- Web: the Flutter Web client offers the same core functions as the mobile apps (registration/login, playback, search, playlist and library management, recommendations, Live Premiere, favorites/ratings/comments, notifications; offline download and video playback where the browser supports them); a Flutter Web admin dashboard offers CRUD operations for songs, albums, artists and user accounts.
- User functions (Requirements Documentation FR-01 to FR-14): registration/login and profile management; music and music-video playback; Live Premiere; rating, comments and favorites; playlist and library management, offline download; search and recommendations; system notifications; in-app purchases through App Store / Google Play billing, where the backend only verifies the store receipt and unlocks the paid feature.
- Supported software: iOS 15.0 and above, Android 8.0 and above, and Chrome 96+, Edge 96+, Firefox 99+ and Safari 15.6+ (the oldest versions Flutter Web runs on) with JavaScript enabled.
- Supported hardware: mobile devices with at least 2 GB RAM, screens of 4.7 to 6.7 inches, resolutions 720p, 1080p and 1440p and aspect ratios 16:9, 18:9 and 20:9; web devices (desktop, laptop or tablet) with at least 2 GB RAM and screens from 1024x768 (768x1024 portrait tablet) up to 1920x1080.
- Server infrastructure: cloud-hosted, containerized backend sized for at least 9,000 concurrent users at launch (up to 15,000 with an error rate < 1%) and horizontally scalable to 50,000 concurrent users in future phases.
Project scope:
- Requirement gathering, system analysis, UI/UX design, frontend and backend development, QA testing (integration, load, security and device), deployment to production, store publishing, administrator training and handover documentation.
- 1-year warranty with technical support and system maintenance after the production deployment.

- 1.1 Requirements and Planning: Project Charter, SRS, Requirements Traceability Matrix with acceptance criteria, Project Scope Statement, WBS and WBS Dictionary.
- 1.2 System and Database Design: system architecture, ER diagram and PostgreSQL schema, detailed design (modules, class and sequence diagrams), general API specification (OpenAPI 3.0), wireframes, high-fidelity mockups and clickable prototype; repository, CI/CD pipeline, staging, backups and CDN.
- 1.3 MVP Development and 1.4 Full Feature Development: source code with unit tests for the backend API, the Live Premiere WebSocket service, the Flutter apps for iOS, Android and Web and the admin dashboard.
- 1.5 Testing and QA: test plan and quality metrics, test cases, integration, load, security and device test reports and the test summary report.
- 1.6 Deployment and Closeout: release candidate on staging, production release with monitoring and backups, apps on the App Store and Google Play, user guide, admin guide and release notes (Vietnamese/English), deployment and operations documentation, administrator training.
- 1.7 Project Management: Project Management Plan (schedule, cost baseline, risk, quality, communications and procurement plans) with the risk register (R-01 to R-12), monthly status and cost reports, final project report.

- Every Must-have and Should-have requirement (FR-01 to FR-14, NFR-01 to NFR-12) meets its acceptance criteria in the Requirements Documentation and passes its RTM verification; Could-have functions (FR-05, FR-10, FR-13) are delivered as capacity allows.
- Load test (1.5.3) with 15,000 virtual users: error rate < 1% and API p90 latency < 200 ms; cold start < 2 s and warm start < 1 s; battery consumption < 6% per hour.
- No open critical (S1) or high (S2) defect at the release candidate (1.5.8); automated backend test coverage >= 70%; restore drill completed within the 4-hour RTO.
- UAT score of at least 4.2/5 and the Customer's acceptance sign-off (1.6.3); crash-free rate >= 99% during hypercare (1.6.5).
- Apps published on the App Store and Google Play; handover deliverables accepted by the Customer (1.6.12); project closure signed by the Sponsor (1.7.9).

- Separate native codebases for iOS and Android; native desktop applications (Windows, macOS, Linux).
- Processing payments directly (own payment gateway, card details, e-wallets such as MoMo, ZaloPay, VNPay).
- Designing music subscription plans and prices (the paid products are defined by the Sponsor).
- GUI languages other than Vietnamese and English.
- Product marketing and user acquisition; music content licensing.
- User Acceptance Testing: planned and performed by the Customer on the staging environment; the team only deploys the release candidate and fixes the defects the Customer reports (1.6.1, 1.6.2).
- Customer support and maintenance after the 1-year warranty period.

- Budget: 757,000,000 VND = cost baseline 720,921,916 VND + management reserve 36,046,096 VND, released only by the Sponsor (Project Charter).
- Schedule: August 17, 2026 - January 15, 2027 (108 working days); the Summary Milestones of the Project Charter; schedule variance of at most 14 days.
- Team: 5 fixed members; each member works on one work package at a time and at most 176 hours in any month.
- Technology: Flutter (single codebase for iOS, Android and Web), Node.js (Express.js), PostgreSQL and WebSocket (Project Charter, Technical Decisions); minimum iOS 15.0, Android 8.0 and the browser versions in the scope description.
- Payments only through App Store / Google Play billing; no card data stored by the system.
- App Store Review Guidelines, Google Play Developer Program Policies and the Vietnamese Law on Personal Data Protection.
- Change control: the PM approves changes of up to 2% of the budget (15,140,000 VND) and up to 3 days of schedule; larger changes go to the Sponsor.

- The Sponsor and the Customer attend the meetings, reviews, demos and sign-offs on the scheduled dates (Assumption Log A-01 to A-12).
- The App Store and Google Play review the apps within 3 working days (A-13); the cloud and CDN accounts are active within 2 working days of the purchase (A-14).
- The requirements collected in 1.1.1 are complete: 14 functions and 12 non-functional requirements.
- The Customer performs UAT on staging from December 23, 2026 and signs the acceptance on January 4, 2027 (A-09).
- The Sponsor defines the paid features sold through in-app purchase.
- The music catalog loaded during the project fits in 1,000 GB of object storage (Resource Requirements PR-03).

• Technical decisions: the Technical Lead (Trần Đình Hiếu) presents the options with their trade-offs; the PM makes the final decision after consulting the technical members (Project Charter, Technical Decisions).

• Step 1 - Direct discussion: the members involved talk privately within 2 working days, focusing on the issue and the facts, not on the person.
• Step 2 - Facilitation: if they do not agree, the PM facilitates a meeting using collaborate / problem-solve first, then compromise.
• Step 3 - Decision: if there is still no agreement, the PM makes the final call, records it and the team commits to it.
